summary_md:
**Liqin Ye ([@liqinye27](https://x.com/liqinye27/status/2115220337302347998))** (Amazon internship work) introduces **AlphaBet**, an agentic RL framework that trains one policy to search, read, reason and forecast real-world events across multiple historical forecast dates, rewarding each forecast against the eventual outcome. The thread reports:

- On GLM-4.5-Air: Forecast-Dojo accuracy 41.6% → 50.5% and FutureX 51.3% → 57.9%, with Brier scores down ~14%.
- Gains come from both better evidence and better probability reporting; other models forecast better using evidence AlphaBet retrieved.
- Std normalization in GRPO distorts proper-scoring-rule targets; AlphaBet keeps mean-centering only.
- Paper, website, code, models and data are released.

referenced_urls.title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents

relevance: RL that improves an agent's research process, not just its final answer.

media.description: AlphaBet method diagram: longitudinal forecasting over an evolving corpus, where an LLM agent uses search, read and compute tools over a date-gated offline corpus and sandbox, optionally keeps a notebook, reports probabilities, and is trained with GRPO without std normalization using negative Brier score rewards.

Scatter plots of Brier score vs accuracy on Forecast-Dojo and FutureX, showing AlphaBet improving GLM-4.5-Air by +8.9 pp accuracy (-14.4% Brier) and +6.6 pp (-13.7% Brier), compared with Sonnet 4.6, Kimi K2.5, Qwen3.5 397B, MiniMax-M2.5, BLF and OpenForecaster.

Table of Brier scores for readers (GPT-5.6 Terra xhigh, Claude Sonnet 4.6 high, GLM-4.5-Air, +AlphaBet memory-free) given base evidence, AlphaBet-gathered evidence, or none, with Δacq and Δreport improvements.

Training curves comparing GRPO with and without std normalization under Brier and log rewards: without normalization Brier falls from 0.731 to 0.668 and log prob improves, while with normalization calibration degrades.
